I need to know what's on the schedule today and how you're feeling right now. You've got no program running yet, so there's no session you're locked into. The real question is whether you can train safely on zero sleep — and that depends on what you're actually feeling. Are you wired, wiped out, shaky, dizzy? No sleep hits everyone differently, and trying to max out lifts or push hard on a run when you're that taxed is a good way to hurt yourself or miss the point entirely.

If you want to move your body today, keep it light: a walk, some easy mobility, maybe technique work at low intensity with light weight. Save the real work for when you've slept. One bad night isn't worth fighting for and it's not worth the injury risk either.
